review.note: Original OathSteps practice material. Reading and writing sentences use words from the USCIS reading and writing vocabulary lists; they are not the sentences used in interviews. Conversation prompts ask for truthful personal answers and never supply them. Not an official English assessment.

sources.label: USCIS: Study for the test (reading and writing vocabulary)

reading.text: What is the capital of the United States?
Why do people come to America?
Who lives in the White House?
What country is north of the United States?
Name one right in the Bill of Rights.
How many senators do we have?
Who can vote in the United States?

writing.text: The President lives in the White House.
Canada is north of the United States.
The flag is red, white, and blue.
Lincoln was President during the Civil War.

instructions.meaning: Lift your right hand; the officer is about to ask you to swear to tell the truth.

instructions.text: Do you promise to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth?
instructions.meaning: Answer “Yes” or “I do” if you agree to tell the truth.

instructions.text: May I see your green card and your passport?
instructions.meaning: Hand the officer your permanent resident card and passport.
Read the sentence the officer shows you, out loud.
Write down the sentence the officer says.
A truthful yes-or-no question about your history. Answer honestly; explain if needed.
Say where you live now, the same as on your application.
It is fine to say “No, could you please repeat it?”
Write your signature where the officer points.

vocabulary.meaning: A person allowed to live and work in the United States permanently (green card holder).
The promise you make to the United States at the naturalization ceremony.
Whether you are single, married, divorced, widowed, or separated.
Any time you left the country, including short visits.
A notice from police or a court, for example for a traffic violation.
People you support financially, such as children.
The U.S. system that registers men aged 18 to 25 for possible military service.

vocabulary.term: Bear arms on behalf of the United States
vocabulary.meaning: To serve in the military and fight for the United States if the law requires it.
Ordered by the government to leave the United States.

conversation.prompt: Tell me about your current job.
conversation.tip: Say your job title and where you work. Use your own true details.

conversation.prompt: How long have you lived at your current address?
conversation.tip: Give the number of years or months, as on your application.

conversation.prompt: Have you traveled outside the United States since you became a permanent resident?
conversation.tip: Answer yes or no, then name the countries and roughly how long, as you listed them.

conversation.prompt: Are you married? Tell me about your spouse.
conversation.tip: State your marital status. If married, say your spouse's name and whether they are a citizen.

conversation.prompt: Why do you want to become a U.S. citizen?
conversation.tip: There is no right answer. Say your own reason in one or two sentences.

conversation.prompt: Do you have any children? Where do they live?
conversation.tip: Say how many and where they live, as on your application.

conversation.prompt: Have you ever failed to file a required tax return?
conversation.tip: Answer truthfully. If something is complicated, say so and explain.

conversation.prompt: Are you willing to take the full Oath of Allegiance?
conversation.tip: Answer yes if you are willing. Ask the officer if you do not understand a part.
